what_it_states: Single real-valued query (dimension one), pure epsilon-DP, global sensitivity Delta (shifts |d| <= Delta), worst-case expected cost of a symmetric nondecreasing cost L with a growth condition (Property 2). Theorem 2 (Appendix A): query-output-independent noise is optimal within piecewise-constant periodic families (conjectured in general). Theorem 3 (Appendix B, eight steps: symmetrization, no atoms/no null intervals, piecewise-constant approximation, monotone rearrangement, periodic decay, step reduction): inf over ALL epsilon-DP noise laws on R equals inf over the one-parameter staircase family f_gamma. Theorem 4: L=|x| gives gamma* = 1/(1+e^{epsilon/2}) and value Delta e^{epsilon/2}/(e^epsilon - 1). Theorem 6: L=x^2 gives gamma* as the real root of an explicit cubic and value Delta^2 (2^{-2/3} b^{2/3}(1+b)^{2/3} + b)/(1-b)^2 with b=e^{-epsilon}. Corollaries 5/7 asymptotics; Theorem 8 / Corollary 9 asymptotic gamma* for moment costs; heuristic gamma=b/2. Discrete setting: Theorem 10 (output-independence within periodic families), Theorem 11 (geometric optimal for Delta=1), Theorem 12 (discrete staircase P_r optimal for Delta>=2). Section VII: abstract staircase achieves 2 epsilon-DP. Section I-D7 remark: for d linear queries, independent per-coordinate staircase noise with parameter epsilon/d achieves an UPPER bound Theta(e^{-epsilon/(3d)} d sqrt d) as epsilon -> infinity.
what_it_does_not_state: No multidimensional all-law optimality (the d-query remark is only an upper bound via independent coordinates with split budget); no l1-diamond or any planar sensitivity body; no squared-Euclidean MSE selector in dimension two; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2; no rounded-core or diamond-core selector; Theorem 3 is an infimum equality over the staircase family and does not itself assert uniqueness of the optimal law among all laws.
relation_to_SOURCE_MATCH_U1: Supplies the one-dimensional all-law MSE (x^2) optimum and its selector gamma* at its own scope (d=1, interval sensitivity). Does not supply T-MATCH for the registered planar l1-diamond model: first failed implication = dimension/sensitivity geometry (scalar interval versus planar l1 diamond), and the multidimensional remark is a non-optimal upper bound. Positive prior credit retained for the scalar staircase framework and the scalar x^2 selector at d=1.
